proposed_widenings.name: companion_creation spell family
proposed_widenings.justification: Animate Dead creates one or more undead companions that persist independently for 24 hours under the caster's control. None of the four existing SpellMechanics families can honestly represent this shape: ongoing_effect requires concentration or a timed duration on the spell itself; activation's Effect union is DamageEffect|NoneEffect with no companion-creation variant; triggered_reaction and anchored_trigger are wrong structural shapes. A new family is needed whose header captures: (a) companion count (fixed or slot-scaled), (b) companion kind (undead, etc.), (c) control interface (Bonus Action mental command, range in feet, multi-target same-order), (d) control duration (24 hours), (e) recast behavior (reassert control over existing creatures up to N, rather than animating new).
proposed_widenings.evidence: The target becomes an Undead creature: a Skeleton if you chose bones or a Zombie if you chose a corpse. On each of your turns, you can take a Bonus Action to mentally command any creature you made with this spell if the creature is within 60 feet of you. The creature is under your control for 24 hours, after which it stops obeying any command you've given it. To maintain control of the creature for another 24 hours, you must cast this spell on the creature again before the current 24-hour period ends. This use of the spell reasserts your control over up to four creatures you have animated with this spell rather than animating a new creature.

proposed_widenings.name: CompanionEffect in the Effect union
proposed_widenings.justification: The Effect type (DamageEffect | NoneEffect) has no variant for companion creation. Even if activation phases were extended, they cannot carry a create_companion result. A CompanionEffect variant (or a dedicated companion_creation family that bypasses phases entirely) is required before the v4 create_companion atom can be traced.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The target becomes an Undead creature: a Skeleton if you chose bones or a Zombie if you chose a corpse.

proposed_widenings.name: control_duration in Duration or a new control_link surface type
proposed_widenings.justification: The spell's Duration is Instantaneous (the cast itself), but the control relationship lasts 24 hours and must be renewed. This is neither concentration nor a timed spell duration. A surface representation of the control_link lifetime (including recast-to-extend semantics) is missing. The v4 command_companion atom is listed in the taxonomy but cannot be traced without a surface type that expresses the control relationship.
proposed_widenings.evidence: To maintain control of the creature for another 24 hours, you must cast this spell on the creature again before the current 24-hour period ends. This use of the spell reasserts your control over up to four creatures you have animated with this spell rather than animating a new creature.

proposed_widenings.name: SlotScaling<number> for companion count
proposed_widenings.justification: Higher-level casting adds +2 creatures per slot above 3. The SlotScaling<T> type exists and is used for target counts (Bless), but there is no surface field on any SpellMechanics family that would hold a slot-scaled companion count. This widening is secondary to the family gap — it would be resolved when the companion_creation family is defined.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You animate or reassert control over two additional Undead creatures for each spell slot level above 3.

notes: The casting time (1 minute, non-ritual) is representable via the existing CastingTime minutes variant. The school (necromancy), level (3), components, and range (10-foot point) all fit existing surface types. The only blocker is structural: no SpellMechanics family exists for companion-creation spells. The v4 taxonomy has both create_companion and command_companion as effect atoms, but neither is reachable without a surface family that can house them. Animate Dead is the archetype for a companion_creation family that would also cover Create Undead, Find Familiar, Find Steed, and similar summoning spells. The recast-to-maintain semantics (reasserting control rather than creating anew, up to a capped count) are a novel pattern not seen in any existing family.
